metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Oktober 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.169

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Oktober 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.169
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.169
- Datum: 10.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear H. & M. I can really confirm that we have here in our little bungalow
absolutely the life I wanted after the strenuous times in New York etc. I have as my
real workroom a large covered terrace in front of the beautiful mountains, the
neighborhood is very primitive and therefore picturesque, the poor people are so nice
here as you cannot imagine; our black housemaid is silent, diligent, clean and
grateful to us as she learns to see things she never has seen in her life - {she begins to sing now} for
them potatoes are already a luxury and fish an unknown animal. She takes our
empty tins at home as a treasure and uses them there as glasses but nevertheless
she is clean and it is the intern civilisation and humanity I admire so much here
in this country. Lotte is busy; you would not believe it as we make very few walks
and see no people that the day runs so quickly away, that we are quite surprised
to be here already three weeks. I am happy that she likes this kind of life as
much as I do; I am only not quite satisfied with her health. She has cheated
me first in having no dowry, now in loosing weight by her demure[?] eating, which
is somewhat better but every night there are one or two dialogues between her and
a dog in a house far away. Whenever she begins to cough the dog begins to bark
as the air is quite still and transmits every sound in a great distance, I
insist that she now makes a cure to get some embonpoint, because here life
is so quiet and easy that I wish she should take provisions for the bad times
which are expecting us in the future. Altogether I cannot tell you how happy
we are to have left New York where our life did not belong to us and we had all
sorts of problems, while here we live forgotten and forgetting the time, the world
(but not you) Fräulein is as always the object of my most fervent admiration,
the earns here with his larger book at least twenty times what I with my book,
having all entrenchous[?], connexions and that was not easy coming here without
to know anybody or a word of Portuguese. How I regret that I did not move
to Brazil five years ago, you have no idea of the fantastic modernity - a house
which was worth 100 £ five years ago cost now 500 or even a thousand, but
life is still cheap, all the native things in excellent quality as people have not
yet learned to use substitutes. And we told you already what we say, overpaying
the usual rates - 5 dollars a month to our maid while in America one has
to pay 60 or 80 and she takes there two holidays a week. I do not generally
be mean, but you understand what a relief it is to know that one can
still live cheaply somewhere and will not be dependent from newspapers and
agents. How you would like this country, so colourful and peaceful in such
a time. - Let me tell you that your letters are expected with the greatest
interest - I hope this winter will not be too hard. Give Hermann my love, I should really write to
him, but it is not the higher postage but the feeling that every letter takes much
longer than one does not so easily [?] love and greetings to all! Stefan
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig auf einem Blatt, beidseitig beschrieben (bzw. Randnotizen). Die Transkription umfasst den Haupttext und die Randnotizen.
Rückseite des Dokuments, zeigt den durchscheinenden Text der Vorderseite. Keine eigenständige Transkription.
Farbskala und Grauskala für Archivierungszwecke über dem Dokument platziert.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Randnotizen, die sich teilweise überlappen. Einige Wörter wie 'entrenchous' sind aufgrund der Handschrift leicht unsicher.
